source.text: אָ֭דָם יְל֣וּד אִשָּׁ֑ה קְצַ֥ר יָ֝מִ֗ים וּֽשְׂבַֽע־רֹֽגֶז׃

records.literal_gloss: A human, born of a woman, [is] short of days and full of turmoil.

en.L: {{gender:A human|Man}}, born of a woman, \q [is] short of days and full of turmoil.
en.B: {{gender:A human being|Man}}, born of a woman, \q lives few days, and those days are full of trouble.
en.R: Every human being is born of a woman. \q Our lives are short and full of trouble.

es.L: {{gender:El ser humano|El hombre}}, nacido de mujer, \q [es] corto de días y harto de inquietud.
es.B: {{gender:El ser humano|El hombre}}, nacido de mujer, \q vive pocos días, y esos días están llenos de angustia.
es.R: Todo ser humano nace de una mujer. \q Nuestra vida es corta y está llena de problemas.

fr.L: {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}}, né de la femme, \q [est] court de jours et rassasié de tourment.
fr.B: {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}}, né d’une femme, \q vit peu de jours, et ces jours sont pleins de tourments.
fr.R: Tout être humain naît d’une femme. \q Notre vie est courte et pleine de soucis.

sw.L: Mwanadamu, mzaliwa wa mwanamke, \q [ni] mfupi wa siku na ameshiba msukosuko.
sw.B: Mwanadamu, aliyezaliwa na mwanamke, \q huishi siku chache, na siku hizo zimejaa dhiki.
sw.R: Kila mwanadamu amezaliwa na mwanamke. \q Maisha yetu ni mafupi na yamejaa matatizo.

vi.L: Con người do người nữ sinh ra \q [thì] ít ngày và no đầy xao động.
vi.B: Con người do người nữ sinh ra \q chỉ sống ít ngày, mà những ngày ấy đầy dẫy rối ren.
vi.R: Mọi người đều do người nữ sinh ra. \q Đời chúng con ngắn ngủi và đầy khổ đau.

ko.L: 여자에게서 난 사람은 \q 날이 짧고 불안으로 가득하다.
ko.B: 여자에게서 태어난 사람은 \q 사는 날이 얼마 되지 않고, 그 날들마저 괴로움으로 가득하다.
ko.R: 사람은 누구나 여자에게서 태어난다. \q 우리 삶은 짧고 괴로움이 가득하다.

decisions.choice: a human, born of a woman: every mortal, frail by birth
decisions.reason: "Born of a woman" stresses human weakness: everyone enters life the same way (15:14; 25:4). Job now speaks of all humankind, not only himself, though his own case runs through the whole poem.

decisions.choice: full of turmoil: having more than enough trouble
decisions.reason: The word for "full" (seva') means satisfied, having had one's fill. Here a short life is filled with turmoil (rogez), the restless trouble of 3:26. At the end of the book Job dies "old and full of days" (42:17), with the same word.

decisions.choice: we, our
decisions.reason: In this chapter Readable speaks of humankind as "we", which includes Job, every reader and both men and women, in place of the Hebrew "he".

decisions.choice: "chúng con" for the Readable "we, our"
decisions.reason: Job's speech from 13:20 to the end of chapter 14 is addressed to God, and in it he calls himself "con". Where Readable speaks of humankind as "we", Vietnamese says "chúng con", which takes in Job and all mortals speaking before God.

decisions.choice: plain 해라체 for the lines about humankind and nature (verses 1-2, 4, 7-12, 18-19a, 21-22, Readable "we" as "우리"); 합쇼체 with "주님" and "저" where Job speaks to God
decisions.reason: The chapter moves between general lines about mortals and direct pleas to God. Korean gives the descriptive and proverbial lines the plain style of written poetry and keeps the 합쇼체 of prayer for the lines addressed to God, as the Psalms move between the two.

source.text: כְּצִ֣יץ יָ֭צָא וַיִּמָּ֑ל וַיִּבְרַ֥ח כַּ֝צֵּ֗ל וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a flower he comes forth and withers; and he flees like the shadow and not stays.

en.L: Like a flower {{gender:they come up and wither|he comes up and withers}}; \q and {{gender:they flee|he flees}} like a shadow and {{gender:do|does}} not stay.
en.B: {{gender:They spring up|He springs up}} like a flower and {{gender:wither|withers}}; \q {{gender:they slip|he slips}} away like a shadow and {{gender:do|does}} not last.
en.R: We bloom like a flower and then dry up. \q We pass like a shadow and are gone.

es.L: Como una flor brota y se marchita; \q y se escapa como una sombra y no se queda.
es.B: Brota como una flor y se marchita; \q se desvanece como una sombra y no perdura.
es.R: Florecemos como una flor y luego nos secamos. \q Pasamos como una sombra y desaparecemos.

fr.L: Comme une fleur il sort et se fane ; \q et il fuit comme l’ombre et ne demeure pas.
fr.B: Il pousse comme une fleur et se fane ; \q il s’efface comme une ombre et ne dure pas.
fr.R: Nous fleurissons comme une fleur, puis nous séchons. \q Nous passons comme une ombre, et nous ne sommes plus là.

sw.L: Kama ua hutokeza na kunyauka; \q hukimbia kama kivuli wala hakai.
sw.B: Huchipuka kama ua kisha hunyauka; \q hupita kama kivuli wala hadumu.
sw.R: Tunachanua kama ua kisha tunakauka. \q Tunapita kama kivuli na kutoweka.

vi.L: Như bông hoa, người mọc lên rồi tàn héo; \q và trốn đi như bóng và không ở lại.
vi.B: Con người nở ra như hoa rồi tàn úa; \q lướt qua như chiếc bóng và chẳng còn lại.
vi.R: Chúng con nở như hoa rồi khô héo. \q Chúng con qua đi như chiếc bóng rồi biến mất.

ko.L: 꽃처럼 피어났다가 시들고, \q 그림자처럼 달아나 머물지 않는다.
ko.B: 사람은 꽃처럼 피었다가 시들고, \q 그림자처럼 사라져 오래가지 못한다.
ko.R: 우리는 꽃처럼 피었다가 말라 버린다. \q 그림자처럼 지나가 사라져 버린다.

decisions.choice: a flower, a shadow: a life that does not last
decisions.reason: A wild flower blooms and soon withers (Psalm 103:15-16; Isaiah 40:6-8); a shadow moves on and is gone (8:9; Psalm 144:4). Both pictures show how brief a human life is.

decisions.choice: withers: dries up, is cut off
decisions.reason: The verb (malal) is used of plants that dry up or are cut off (18:16; Psalm 37:2). Either way the flower is soon gone.

source.text: אַף־עַל־זֶ֭ה פָּקַ֣חְתָּ עֵינֶ֑ךָ וְאֹ֘תִ֤י תָבִ֖יא בְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Even on this [one] do you open your eyes, and me do you bring into judgment with you?

en.L: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} even open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes on such a one? \q And do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring me into judgment with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.B: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} really fix {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes on such a one? \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring me to trial before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.R: Is someone like this worth {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} close watch? \q Must {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} drag me into court with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?

es.L: ¿Aun sobre uno así abres {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos? \q ¿Y a mí me llevas a juicio frente a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?
es.B: ¿De veras fijas {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos en alguien así? \q ¿Me llevarás a juicio delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?
es.R: ¿Merece alguien así que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo vigiles tan de cerca? \q ¿Tienes que arrastrarme a un juicio delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?

fr.L: Même sur un tel [être] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ouvres {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux ? \q Et moi, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’amènes en jugement avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ?
fr.B: Est-ce vraiment sur un tel être que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fixes {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux ? \q Vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me faire passer en jugement devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ?
fr.R: Quelqu’un comme lui mérite-t-il que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le surveilles de si près ? \q Faut-il que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me traînes au tribunal devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ?

sw.L: Je, hata juu ya mtu kama huyu unafumbua macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}? \q Na mimi unanileta hukumuni pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}?
sw.B: Je, kweli unamkazia macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mtu kama huyu? \q Utanileta mahakamani mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?
sw.R: Je, mtu kama huyu anastahili {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umchunguze kwa karibu hivyo? \q Je, ni lazima unikokote mahakamani mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?

vi.L: Chúa lại mở mắt trên một kẻ như thế sao? \q Và đem con vào sự xét xử với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sao?
vi.B: Chúa thật sự để mắt dò xét một kẻ như thế sao? \q Ngài sẽ đem con ra xử trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sao?
vi.R: Một người như thế có đáng để Chúa canh chừng sát sao không? \q Chúa có cần lôi con ra tòa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không?

ko.L: 이런 자에게도 주님께서 눈을 뜨십니까? \q 그리고 저를 주님과 함께 심판에 들이십니까?
ko.B: 이런 자에게서 정말 눈을 떼지 않으십니까? \q 저를 주님 앞에 세워 재판하시렵니까?
ko.R: 이런 사람이 주님께서 그렇게 꼼꼼히 지켜보실 만한 존재입니까? \q 꼭 저를 법정으로 끌고 가셔야 합니까?

decisions.choice: open your eyes on: watch closely, keep under scrutiny
decisions.reason: To open one's eyes on someone is to watch them closely. Job has already asked why God keeps such close watch on a mere human (7:17-20; 13:27). "This one" is the short-lived mortal of verses 1-2.

decisions.choice: me ... with you: Job applies it to himself
decisions.reason: Job moves from "such a one" to "me": the frail human God is watching is Job himself, and God is bringing him to trial. "With you" means as the other party in the case.

decisions.choice: Is someone like this worth your close watch?
alternatives: Do you open your eyes on such a one?
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the sense of the question, that a mortal is too small to be worth such scrutiny (m1).

decisions.choice: Job to God: "Chúa" and "Ngài", "con" for himself
decisions.reason: As in Job's earlier pleas, he addresses God as the Psalms' laments do. His speech is bitter, and "tôi" would sound harder; "con" keeps the relation of a mortal before God while the words themselves carry the protest.

source.text: מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן טָ֭הוֹר מִטָּמֵ֗א לֹ֣א אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will give a clean [thing] from an unclean? Not one.

en.L: Who can bring a clean [thing] out of an unclean? \q Not one.
en.B: Who can bring what is clean out of what is unclean? \q No one!
en.R: Can anyone make something clean out of something unclean? \q No one can!

es.L: ¿Quién dará algo puro de lo impuro? \q Ni uno solo.
es.B: ¿Quién puede sacar lo puro de lo impuro? \q ¡Nadie!
es.R: ¿Puede alguien convertir algo impuro en algo puro? \q ¡Nadie puede!

fr.L: Qui tirera du pur de l’impur ? \q Pas un.
fr.B: Qui peut tirer ce qui est pur de ce qui est impur ? \q Personne !
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut-il rendre pur ce qui est impur ? \q Personne ne le peut !

sw.L: Nani atatoa kitu safi kutoka kwa kitu kichafu? \q Hakuna hata mmoja.
sw.B: Ni nani awezaye kutoa kilicho safi katika kilicho najisi? \q Hakuna!
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu anayeweza kufanya kitu kichafu kiwe safi? \q Hakuna anayeweza!

vi.L: Ai sẽ đem [vật] tinh sạch ra từ [vật] ô uế? \q Không một ai.
vi.B: Ai có thể lấy cái thanh sạch ra từ cái ô uế? \q Chẳng ai cả!
vi.R: Có ai làm được cho điều ô uế trở nên tinh sạch không? \q Không ai làm được!

ko.L: 누가 부정한 것에서 깨끗한 것을 내겠는가? \q 하나도 없다.
ko.B: 누가 더러운 것에서 깨끗한 것을 낼 수 있겠는가? \q 아무도 없다!
ko.R: 더러운 것을 깨끗하게 만들 수 있는 사람이 있는가? \q 아무도 없다!

decisions.choice: Who will give: who can bring about
alternatives: Oh that a clean thing could come from an unclean!
decisions.reason: The words "who will give" can be a real question, "who can produce?", or the usual Hebrew wish, "oh that ...!" (as in 13:5 and 14:13). Read as a question, with "not one" as its answer, Job says no mortal can be pure. Read as a wish, he longs for what cannot happen. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: clean, unclean: pure and impure
decisions.reason: The words are those of the law of clean and unclean (Leviticus 11-15), used here of human nature. A being born of a woman (verse 1) cannot be pure before God (15:14; 25:4). Job may mean that God should not expect from him what no mortal can give.

source.text: אִ֥ם חֲרוּצִ֨ים׀יָמָ֗יו מִֽסְפַּר־חֳדָשָׁ֥יו אִתָּ֑ךְ חֻקָּ֥יו עָ֝שִׂ֗יתָ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: If determined [are] his days, the number of his months [is] with you; his limits you have made, and not he will pass [them],

en.L: If {{gender:their|his}} days are determined, \q the number of {{gender:their|his}} months [is] with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{gender:their|his}} limits {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set, and {{gender:they|he}} cannot pass [them],
en.B: Since {{gender:their|his}} days are fixed, \q and the number of {{gender:their|his}} months is in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands, \q since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set limits that {{gender:they|he}} cannot cross,
en.R: You have already decided how long each of us will live. \q You know the number of our months. \q You have set limits we cannot go beyond.

es.L: Si sus días están determinados, \q el número de sus meses [está] junto a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has fijado sus límites, y no [los] podrá pasar,
es.B: Ya que sus días están fijados \q y el número de sus meses está en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos, \q ya que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} le has puesto límites que no puede cruzar,
es.R: Ya decidiste cuánto vivirá cada uno de nosotros. \q Conoces el número de nuestros meses. \q Pusiste límites que no podemos traspasar.

fr.L: Si ses jours sont fixés, \q le nombre de ses mois [est] auprès de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as posé ses limites, et il ne [les] franchira pas,
fr.B: Puisque ses jours sont fixés \q et que le nombre de ses mois est entre {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains, \q puisque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as posé des limites qu’il ne peut franchir,
fr.R: Tu as déjà décidé combien de temps chacun de nous vivra. \q Tu connais le nombre de nos mois. \q Tu as fixé des limites que nous ne pouvons pas dépasser.

sw.L: Ikiwa siku zake zimeamuliwa, \q hesabu ya miezi yake [iko] {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}; \q umeweka mipaka yake, naye hawezi kuivuka,
sw.B: Kwa kuwa siku zake zimepangwa, \q na hesabu ya miezi yake iko mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}, \q kwa kuwa umemwekea mipaka asiyoweza kuivuka,
sw.R: Tayari umeamua kila mmoja wetu ataishi muda gani. \q Unajua hesabu ya miezi yetu. \q Umeweka mipaka ambayo hatuwezi kuivuka.

vi.L: Nếu ngày tháng của họ đã được định, \q số tháng của họ [ở] nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q Chúa đã đặt giới hạn cho họ, và họ không thể vượt qua,
vi.B: Vì ngày tháng con người đã được định, \q số tháng của họ ở trong tay Chúa, \q vì Chúa đã đặt ra giới hạn mà họ không thể vượt qua,
vi.R: Chúa đã định sẵn mỗi người chúng con sống được bao lâu. \q Chúa biết số tháng của chúng con. \q Chúa đã đặt giới hạn mà chúng con không thể vượt qua.

ko.L: 그의 날들이 정해져 있고, \q 그의 달 수가 주님께 있으며, \q 주님께서 그의 한계를 정하셔서 그가 [그것을] 넘지 못한다면,
ko.B: 사람의 날이 이미 정해져 있고 \q 그 달 수가 주님의 손에 있으며, \q 주님께서 그가 넘을 수 없는 한계를 정해 두셨으니,
ko.R: 주님께서는 저희 각 사람이 얼마나 살지 이미 정하셨습니다. \q 저희가 살 달 수를 알고 계십니다. \q 저희가 넘을 수 없는 한계를 정해 두셨습니다.

decisions.choice: If: since, as is the case
decisions.reason: "If" here states what is true, not a doubt: since God has fixed the length of each life. The conclusion follows in verse 6.

decisions.choice: determined, limits: the span of life set by God
decisions.reason: The first word (charuts) means cut, decided, decreed. The second (choq) is a fixed limit, as God sets the sea its limit (38:10). The written text has "his limit" in the singular; it is read as plural, "his limits". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: with you: known to you and in your control
decisions.reason: The number of a person's months is "with" God: he knows it and holds it. Psalm 39:5-6 and 90:10 speak of the same measured span.

decisions.choice: a full stop at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 6. Literal and Balanced end with a comma; Readable makes verse 5 its own sentences and starts verse 6 with "So".

source.text: שְׁעֵ֣ה מֵעָלָ֣יו וְיֶחְדָּ֑ל עַד־יִ֝רְצֶ֗ה כְּשָׂכִ֥יר יוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look away from on him, that he may cease, until he enjoys like a hired laborer his day.

en.L: look away from {{gender:them|him}}, that {{gender:they|he}} may rest, \q until {{gender:they complete their|he completes his}} day like a hired laborer.
en.B: then look away from {{gender:them|him}} and let {{gender:them|him}} rest, \q until, like a hired worker, {{gender:they finish their|he finishes his}} day.
en.R: So stop watching us and leave us alone, \q until we have finished our day like a worker hired for the day.

es.L: aparta [la mirada] de él, para que descanse, \q hasta que cumpla su día como un jornalero.
es.B: entonces aparta de él la mirada y déjalo descansar, \q hasta que, como un jornalero, termine su jornada.
es.R: Así que deja de vigilarnos y déjanos en paz, \q hasta que terminemos nuestro día como el trabajador que cobra por día.

fr.L: détourne-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de lui, pour qu’il ait du repos, \q jusqu’à ce qu’il achève sa journée comme un journalier.
fr.B: alors détourne de lui {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} regard et laisse-le se reposer, \q jusqu’à ce qu’il termine sa journée, comme un ouvrier payé à la journée.
fr.R: Alors arrête de nous surveiller et laisse-nous tranquilles, \q jusqu’à ce que nous ayons fini notre journée, comme un ouvrier engagé pour un jour.

sw.L: geuza macho kutoka kwake, ili apumzike, \q hadi aimalize siku yake kama mfanyakazi wa kuajiriwa.
sw.B: basi uache kumtazama, umwache apumzike, \q mpaka, kama kibarua, aimalize siku yake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo acha kutuangalia, utuache tupumzike, \q mpaka tumalize siku yetu kama kibarua aliyeajiriwa kwa siku moja.

vi.L: xin quay mắt khỏi họ, để họ được nghỉ, \q cho đến khi họ làm trọn ngày mình như người làm thuê.
vi.B: thì xin Chúa thôi nhìn họ và để họ yên nghỉ, \q cho đến khi họ xong ngày công như người làm thuê.
vi.R: Vậy xin Chúa thôi canh chừng chúng con và để chúng con yên, \q cho đến khi chúng con làm xong ngày của mình như người làm công nhật.

ko.L: 그에게서 [눈을] 돌이키셔서 그가 쉬게 하십시오, \q 그가 품꾼처럼 자기 날을 채울 때까지.
ko.B: 그가 품꾼처럼 하루를 다 마칠 때까지 \q 그에게서 눈을 돌리시어 그를 쉬게 해 주십시오.
ko.R: 그러니 저희를 그만 지켜보시고 내버려 두십시오. \q 하루 품삯을 받는 일꾼처럼 저희가 하루를 다 마칠 때까지 말입니다.

decisions.choice: look away: turn your gaze off him
decisions.reason: Job asked the same of God for himself in 7:19 with the same verb. God's watching feels to him like a guard's, not a friend's.

decisions.choice: that he may cease: rest, be left in peace
decisions.reason: The verb (chadal) means to stop or leave off. Job asks that the mortal may at least have rest. The same verb comes again in verse 7, where the tree's shoots "will not cease".

decisions.choice: until he completes his day: until he has worked out his time
alternatives: until he can enjoy his day
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsah) usually means to take pleasure in, but it can also mean to pay off or complete a term (Leviticus 26:34). Job pictures a hired worker who longs for evening (7:1-2): let the mortal finish his day in peace, or at least enjoy its end.

decisions.choice: the "until" line comes first
alternatives: Hebrew order, with the "until" clause after the request
decisions.reason: A Korean time clause with "때까지" stands before the verb it limits; Balanced puts it first so the request ends the sentence, while Literal keeps the Hebrew order as a trailing phrase.

source.text: כִּ֤י יֵ֥שׁ לָעֵ֗ץ תִּ֫קְוָ֥ה אִֽם־יִ֭כָּרֵת וְע֣וֹד יַחֲלִ֑יף וְ֝יֹֽנַקְתּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א תֶחְדָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For there is for a tree hope: if it is cut down, and again it will sprout, and its shoot not will cease.

en.L: For there is hope for a tree: \q if it is cut down, it will sprout again, \q and its shoots will not cease.
en.B: For a tree there is hope: \q if it is cut down, it will sprout again, \q and its new shoots will not fail.
en.R: At least there is hope for a tree. \q If it is cut down, it will grow again, \q and new shoots will keep coming.

es.L: Porque para el árbol hay esperanza: \q si es cortado, aún retoñará, \q y sus brotes no cesarán.
es.B: Para un árbol hay esperanza: \q si lo cortan, vuelve a brotar, \q y no le faltan nuevos retoños.
es.R: Al menos hay esperanza para un árbol. \q Si lo cortan, vuelve a crecer, \q y le siguen saliendo brotes nuevos.

fr.L: Car il y a pour l’arbre une espérance : \q s’il est coupé, il repoussera encore, \q et ses rejetons ne cesseront pas.
fr.B: Pour un arbre, il y a de l’espoir : \q si on l’abat, il repart, \q et ses jeunes pousses ne manquent pas.
fr.R: Pour un arbre, au moins, il y a de l’espoir. \q Si on le coupe, il recommence à pousser, \q et de nouvelles pousses continuent de sortir.

sw.L: Kwa maana mti una tumaini: \q hata ukikatwa, utatoa machipukizi upya, \q wala vichipukizi vyake havitakwisha.
sw.B: Mti una matumaini: \q ukikatwa, huota tena, \q na machipukizi mapya hayaishi.
sw.R: Angalau mti una tumaini. \q Ukikatwa, unakua tena, \q na machipukizi mapya yanaendelea kutokea.

vi.L: Vì có hy vọng cho cây: \q nếu bị chặt, nó sẽ lại đâm chồi, \q và chồi non của nó sẽ không dứt.
vi.B: Một cái cây còn có hy vọng: \q dù bị đốn, nó vẫn nảy chồi lại, \q và những chồi non chẳng thiếu.
vi.R: Ít ra một cái cây còn có hy vọng. \q Nếu bị chặt, nó lại mọc lên, \q và chồi non cứ tiếp tục nhú ra.

ko.L: 나무에게는 희망이 있다. \q 베일지라도 다시 새싹을 내고, \q 그 햇순이 그치지 않는다.
ko.B: 나무는 그래도 희망이 있다. \q 잘려도 다시 움이 돋고, \q 새 가지가 끊이지 않고 자란다.
ko.R: 적어도 나무에게는 희망이 있다. \q 베어져도 다시 자라나고, \q 새순이 계속 돋아난다.

decisions.choice: hope: an expected future
decisions.reason: The word (tiqvah) runs through Job's speeches (6:8; 7:6; 17:15). Here a tree has a hope that a human being does not seem to have. The chapter ends with God destroying human hope (verse 19).

decisions.choice: sprout again: put out new growth
decisions.reason: The verb (chalaf, in this form) means to change, renew, sprout afresh. It comes from the same root as "relief" in verse 14, the change Job longs for in his own case.

decisions.choice: shoots: young sucker shoots
decisions.reason: The word (yoneqet) means a young shoot, literally a "suckling", growing from a cut stump or root (Psalm 80:12; Hosea 14:7).

source.text: אִם־יַזְקִ֣ין בָּאָ֣רֶץ שָׁרְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בֶעָפָ֗ר יָמ֥וּת גִּזְעֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: If grows old in the earth its root, and in the dust dies its stump,

en.L: Though its root grows old in the earth \q and its stump dies in the dust,
en.B: Even if its root grows old in the ground \q and its stump dies in the dust,
en.R: Its roots may grow old in the ground, \q and its stump may seem dead in the dry soil,

es.L: Aunque envejezca en la tierra su raíz \q y en el polvo muera su tocón,
es.B: Aunque su raíz envejezca en el suelo \q y su tronco muera en el polvo,
es.R: Sus raíces pueden envejecer en la tierra, \q y su tocón puede parecer muerto en el suelo seco,

fr.L: Même si sa racine vieillit dans la terre \q et que dans la poussière meurt sa souche,
fr.B: Même si sa racine vieillit dans le sol \q et que sa souche meurt dans la poussière,
fr.R: Ses racines peuvent vieillir dans le sol, \q et sa souche peut sembler morte dans la terre sèche,

sw.L: Ingawa mzizi wake huzeeka ardhini \q na kisiki chake hufa mavumbini,
sw.B: Hata kama mzizi wake utazeeka ardhini \q na kisiki chake kufa katika mavumbi,
sw.R: Mizizi yake inaweza kuzeeka ardhini, \q na kisiki chake kuonekana kimekufa katika udongo mkavu,

vi.L: Dù rễ nó già cỗi trong đất \q và gốc nó chết trong bụi,
vi.B: Dù rễ nó già cỗi dưới đất \q và gốc cây chết khô trong bụi,
vi.R: Rễ của nó có thể già đi trong đất, \q và gốc nó có vẻ đã chết trong đất khô,

ko.L: 그 뿌리가 땅속에서 늙고 \q 그 그루터기가 흙 속에서 죽을지라도,
ko.B: 그 뿌리가 땅속에서 늙고 \q 그루터기가 흙에서 죽는다 해도,
ko.R: 뿌리가 땅속에서 늙어 가고 \q 그루터기가 마른 흙 속에서 죽은 것처럼 보여도,

decisions.choice: stump: what is left when a tree is cut down
decisions.reason: The word (geza') is the stump or stock of a tree (Isaiah 11:1; 40:24). Even when it looks dead, life remains in it.

decisions.choice: dust: also the place of the dead
decisions.reason: "Dust" is where the dead lie (7:21; 17:16). Job chooses words that fit a tree and a human body alike, preparing for verse 10.

decisions.choice: may seem dead
decisions.reason: Readable says "seem dead" because the stump comes back to life in verse 9; the Hebrew "dies" describes how it looks.

source.text: מֵרֵ֣יחַ מַ֣יִם יַפְרִ֑חַ וְעָשָׂ֖ה קָצִ֣יר כְּמוֹ־נָֽטַע׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] scent of water it will bud and will make branches like a plant.

en.L: at the scent of water it will bud \q and put forth branches like a plant.
en.B: at the first scent of water it will bud \q and put out shoots like a young plant.
en.R: but as soon as it smells water, it buds \q and grows branches like a new plant.

es.L: por el olor del agua echará brotes \q y hará ramas como una planta.
es.B: con solo oler el agua, retoña \q y echa vástagos como un arbolito.
es.R: pero en cuanto huele el agua, echa brotes \q y le crecen ramas como a una planta joven.

fr.L: à l’odeur de l’eau il bourgeonnera \q et produira des branches comme un plant.
fr.B: dès qu’il sent l’eau, il bourgeonne \q et fait des pousses comme un arbuste qu’on vient de planter.
fr.R: mais dès qu’il sent l’eau, il fait des bourgeons \q et ses branches poussent comme celles d’une nouvelle plante.

sw.L: kwa harufu ya maji utatoa vitumba \q na kufanya matawi kama mmea.
sw.B: mara unaponusa maji huchipua \q na kutoa machipukizi kama mmea mchanga.
sw.R: lakini mara tu unaponusa maji, unachipua \q na kuota matawi kama mmea mpya.

vi.L: gặp hơi nước nó sẽ đâm chồi \q và trổ cành như cây [non].
vi.B: vừa ngửi thấy nước, nó liền nảy lộc \q và đâm nhánh như cây non.
vi.R: nhưng ngay khi gặp nước, nó lại nảy lộc \q và mọc cành như một cây mới.

ko.L: 물 냄새에 싹이 돋고 \q 어린나무처럼 가지를 낸다.
ko.B: 물 냄새만 맡아도 움이 트고 \q 갓 심은 나무처럼 새 가지를 뻗는다.
ko.R: 물기만 닿으면 곧 싹이 트고 \q 어린나무처럼 가지가 자란다.

decisions.choice: scent of water: the least touch of moisture
decisions.reason: The tree is pictured as catching the smell of water, as a living creature would. A little water is enough to bring it back.

decisions.choice: a plant: a young, newly planted tree
decisions.reason: The word (neta') means something planted, a sapling. The old stump grows like a young tree again.

source.text: וְגֶ֣בֶר יָ֭מוּת וַֽיֶּחֱלָ֑שׁ וַיִּגְוַ֖ע אָדָ֣ם וְאַיּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man dies and is laid low; and a human expires, and where [is] he?

en.L: But {{gender:a mortal|a man}} dies and is laid low; \q a human expires, and where [is] {{gender:that one|he}}?
en.B: But {{gender:a mortal|a man}} dies and lies powerless; \q a human being breathes {{gender:their|his}} last, and where {{gender:are they|is he}}?
en.R: But we human beings die, and all our strength is gone. \q We breathe our last, and where are we then?

es.L: Pero {{gender:el mortal|el hombre}} muere y queda postrado; \q expira el ser humano, ¿y dónde [está]?
es.B: Pero {{gender:el mortal|el hombre}} muere y queda sin fuerzas; \q el ser humano da su último aliento, ¿y dónde está?
es.R: Pero nosotros, los seres humanos, morimos y se nos acaba toda la fuerza. \q Damos el último suspiro, ¿y dónde estamos entonces?

fr.L: Mais {{gender:le mortel|l’homme}} meurt et gît abattu ; \q l’humain expire, et où [est]-il ?
fr.B: Mais {{gender:le mortel|l’homme}} meurt et reste sans force ; \q l’être humain rend son dernier souffle, et où est-il ?
fr.R: Mais nous, les humains, nous mourons, et toute notre force s’en va. \q Nous rendons notre dernier souffle, et alors, où sommes-nous ?

sw.L: Lakini mtu hufa na kulala chini; \q mwanadamu hukata roho, naye yuko wapi?
sw.B: Lakini mtu hufa na kubaki bila nguvu; \q mwanadamu hutoa pumzi yake ya mwisho, naye yuko wapi?
sw.R: Lakini sisi wanadamu tunakufa, na nguvu zetu zote zinaisha. \q Tunavuta pumzi ya mwisho, na kisha tuko wapi?

vi.L: Còn con người chết đi và nằm xuống bất lực; \q loài người tắt hơi, rồi [họ] ở đâu?
vi.B: Nhưng con người chết đi thì nằm đó bất lực; \q con người trút hơi thở cuối cùng, rồi họ ở đâu?
vi.R: Nhưng loài người chúng con chết đi, mọi sức lực đều tiêu tan. \q Chúng con trút hơi thở cuối cùng, rồi chúng con ở đâu?

ko.L: 그러나 사람은 죽어 쓰러지고, \q 인생은 숨을 거두니, 그가 어디 [있는가]?
ko.B: 그러나 사람은 죽으면 힘없이 누워 버리고, \q 숨을 거두고 나면 그가 어디에 있는가?
ko.R: 그러나 우리 사람은 죽고, 모든 힘이 사라진다. \q 마지막 숨을 거두면, 그때 우리는 어디에 있는가?

decisions.choice: But: the human is set against the tree
decisions.reason: The tree of verses 7-9 has hope; the human being does not. The contrast is the point of the passage.

decisions.choice: a man, a human: even the strongest is mortal
decisions.reason: The first word (gever) means a man in his strength; the second ('adam) is a human being. Strong or weak, all die.

decisions.choice: laid low: weakened, powerless
decisions.reason: The verb (chalash) means to be weak or overpowered (Exodus 17:13). In death a person lies without strength.

decisions.choice: where is he?: gone without trace
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer; the dead are gone and are not seen again on earth (7:8-10; 20:7).

source.text: אָֽזְלוּ־מַ֭יִם מִנִּי־יָ֑ם וְ֝נָהָ֗ר יֶחֱרַ֥ב וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Disappear waters from a sea, and a river dries up and is dry,

en.L: Waters vanish from [the] sea, \q and a river runs dry and is dried up;
en.B: As water vanishes from a lake \q and a river dries up and is parched,
en.R: Water evaporates from a lake, \q and a river dries up and is gone.

es.L: Las aguas se van del mar, \q y el río se agota y se seca;
es.B: Como el agua desaparece de un lago \q y un río se agota y queda reseco,
es.R: El agua de un lago se evapora, \q y un río se seca y desaparece.

fr.L: Les eaux s’en vont de la mer, \q et le fleuve tarit et se dessèche ;
fr.B: Comme l’eau disparaît d’un lac \q et qu’un fleuve tarit et se dessèche,
fr.R: L’eau d’un lac s’évapore, \q et un fleuve s’assèche et disparaît.

sw.L: Maji hutoweka baharini, \q na mto hupwa na kukauka;
sw.B: Kama maji yanavyotoweka ziwani \q na mto kupwa na kukauka kabisa,
sw.R: Maji ya ziwa hukauka kwa jua, \q na mto hukauka na kutoweka.

vi.L: Nước biến khỏi biển, \q và sông cạn và khô đi;
vi.B: Như nước rút khỏi hồ, \q như dòng sông cạn kiệt và khô nứt,
vi.R: Nước trong hồ bốc hơi, \q và dòng sông khô cạn rồi mất đi.

ko.L: 물이 바다에서 사라지고, \q 강이 줄어들어 마르듯이,
ko.B: 호수에서 물이 빠져 버리고 \q 강이 줄어들어 바싹 마르듯이,
ko.R: 호수의 물이 말라 버린다. \q 강도 바싹 말라 사라진다.

decisions.choice: waters vanish, a river dries up: the same words as Isaiah 19:5
decisions.reason: Isaiah 19:5 has almost the same words about the Nile drying up. Here they are a picture of the human being in verse 12: as water is gone and does not come back, so is a life.

decisions.choice: sea: a large body of water, such as a lake
decisions.reason: The word (yam) is the sea, but it is also used of a lake or a great river (Isaiah 19:5). Water that dries up suggests a lake or a pool rather than the ocean.

decisions.choice: As
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "As" to show that this is a comparison, completed by "so" in verse 12 (m1).

source.text: וְאִ֥ישׁ שָׁכַ֗ב וְֽלֹא־יָ֫ק֥וּם עַד־בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝עֹ֗רוּ מִשְּׁנָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man lies down and not rises; until [the] heavens [are] not, not they will awake, and not they will be roused from their sleep.

en.L: so {{gender:a person|a man}} lies down and does not rise; \q until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, \q and they will not be roused from their sleep.
en.B: so {{gender:a person|a man}} lies down and does not rise again; \q until the heavens are gone, the dead will not awake \q or be roused from their sleep.
en.R: In the same way, we lie down in death and do not get up. \q As long as the sky is there, the dead will not wake up \q or be stirred from their sleep.

es.L: así {{gender:la persona|el hombre}} se acuesta y no se levanta; \q hasta que no haya cielos, no despertarán, \q ni serán despertados de su sueño.
es.B: así {{gender:la persona|el hombre}} se acuesta y no vuelve a levantarse; \q mientras existan los cielos, los muertos no despertarán \q ni saldrán de su sueño.
es.R: Así también nosotros nos acostamos en la muerte y no nos levantamos. \q Mientras exista el cielo, los muertos no despertarán \q ni nadie los sacará de su sueño.

fr.L: ainsi {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} se couche et ne se relève pas ; \q jusqu’à ce que les cieux ne soient plus, ils ne s’éveilleront pas, \q et ils ne seront pas tirés de leur sommeil.
fr.B: ainsi {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} se couche et ne se relève plus ; \q tant que les cieux dureront, les morts ne s’éveilleront pas \q et ne sortiront pas de leur sommeil.
fr.R: De même, nous nous couchons dans la mort et nous ne nous relevons pas. \q Tant que le ciel sera là, les morts ne se réveilleront pas \q et personne ne les tirera de leur sommeil.

sw.L: ndivyo mtu hulala wala hainuki; \q mpaka mbingu zisiwepo, hawataamka, \q wala hawataamshwa kutoka usingizini mwao.
sw.B: ndivyo mtu hulala chini wala hainuki tena; \q mpaka mbingu zitoweke, wafu hawataamka \q wala kuamshwa usingizini mwao.
sw.R: Vivyo hivyo tunalala katika kifo na hatuinuki. \q Muda wote anga lipo, wafu hawataamka \q wala kuamshwa kutoka usingizini.

vi.L: thì con người nằm xuống và không trỗi dậy; \q cho đến khi các tầng trời không còn, họ sẽ không thức dậy, \q và sẽ không bị đánh thức khỏi giấc ngủ của họ.
vi.B: con người cũng vậy, nằm xuống rồi không trỗi dậy nữa; \q cho đến khi trời không còn, người chết sẽ không thức giấc, \q cũng chẳng ra khỏi giấc ngủ của mình.
vi.R: Chúng con cũng vậy, nằm xuống trong cõi chết và không đứng dậy. \q Bao lâu bầu trời còn đó, người chết sẽ không thức dậy, \q cũng không ai đánh thức họ khỏi giấc ngủ.

ko.L: 사람도 눕고 일어나지 못한다. \q 하늘이 없어지기까지 그들은 깨지 못하고, \q 잠에서 일으켜지지 못한다.
ko.B: 사람도 누우면 다시 일어나지 못한다. \q 하늘이 다할 때까지 죽은 사람들은 깨어나지 못하고 \q 잠에서 일어나지 못한다.
ko.R: 우리도 죽음 속에 누우면 일어나지 못한다. \q 하늘이 있는 한 죽은 사람들은 깨어나지 못하고 \q 누구도 그들을 잠에서 깨우지 못한다.

decisions.choice: lie down, sleep: death
decisions.reason: Lying down and sleeping are common pictures of death (3:13; 7:21; Psalm 13:4). The one who lies down this way does not get up again in this life.

decisions.choice: until the heavens are no more: never
decisions.reason: The heavens stand for what lasts as long as anything does (Psalm 72:5, 7; Jeremiah 31:35-36). To say the dead will not wake until the heavens are gone is to say they will never wake in the ordinary course of things.

decisions.choice: they will not awake: Job sees no waking from death
decisions.reason: Job speaks of what can be seen: the dead do not return. Yet in the next verses he reaches for a hope beyond death (verses 13-15). Later Scripture uses the same verb "awake" for the dead rising (Isaiah 26:19; Daniel 12:2).

decisions.choice: the dead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name "the dead" as the subject of the plural verbs, since "they" has no plural word before it to refer to.

decisions.choice: lie down in death
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in death" to make the picture plain (m1).

source.text: מִ֤י יִתֵּ֨ן׀בִּשְׁא֬וֹל תַּצְפִּנֵ֗נִי תַּ֭סְתִּירֵנִי עַד־שׁ֣וּב אַפֶּ֑ךָ תָּ֤שִׁ֥יתלִ֖י חֹ֣ק וְתִזְכְּרֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will give [that] in Sheol you would hide me, you would conceal me until turns back your anger, you would set for me a limit and remember me!

en.L: Oh that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would hide me in Sheol, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would conceal me until {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger turns back, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would set me a limit and remember me!
en.B: If only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would hide me in Sheol \q and keep me out of sight until {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger has passed, \q then set a time for me and remember me!
en.R: I wish {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would hide me in the grave \q and keep me there until {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are no longer angry. \q Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} could set a time and remember me.

es.L: ¡Quién diera que en el Seol me escondieras, \q que me ocultaras hasta que se aparte {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira, \q que me fijaras un plazo y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acordaras de mí!
es.B: ¡Si tan solo me escondieras en el lugar de los muertos \q y me guardaras oculto hasta que pase {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enojo, \q y luego me fijaras un tiempo y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acordaras de mí!
es.R: Ojalá me escondieras en el lugar de los muertos \q y me dejaras allí hasta que ya no estés enojado. \q Entonces podrías fijar un tiempo y acordarte de mí.

fr.L: Oh ! si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me cachais dans le Shéol, \q si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’abritais jusqu’à ce que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère se détourne, \q si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fixais une limite et {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} souvenais de moi !
fr.B: Si seulement {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me cachais dans le séjour des morts \q et me gardais à l’abri jusqu’à ce que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère soit passée, \q puis me fixais un moment et {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} souvenais de moi !
fr.R: J’aimerais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me caches dans le séjour des morts \q et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’y gardes jusqu’à ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sois plus en colère. \q Ensuite {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pourrais fixer un moment et {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} souvenir de moi.

sw.L: Lo, kama ungenifunika Kuzimu, \q ungenitunza mafichoni mpaka hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} irudi nyuma, \q ungeniwekea kikomo kisha unikumbuke!
sw.B: Ningependa unifiche Kuzimu \q na kunihifadhi mafichoni mpaka hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ipite, \q kisha uniwekee wakati na kunikumbuka!
sw.R: Natamani ungenificha Kuzimu \q na kuniweka huko mpaka usiwe na hasira tena. \q Kisha ungeweza kuweka wakati na kunikumbuka.

vi.L: Ôi, ước gì Chúa giấu con trong Âm Phủ, \q che khuất con cho đến khi cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nguôi đi, \q đặt cho con một giới hạn và nhớ đến con!
vi.B: Ước gì Chúa giấu con trong Âm Phủ, \q giữ con khuất mắt cho đến khi cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua đi, \q rồi định cho con một thời hạn và nhớ lại con!
vi.R: Con mong Chúa giấu con trong nơi của người chết \q và giữ con ở đó cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết giận. \q Rồi Chúa có thể định một thời điểm và nhớ đến con.

ko.L: 주님께서 저를 스올에 감추시고, \q 주님의 진노가 돌아설 때까지 저를 숨기시며, \q 저를 위해 기한을 정하시고 저를 기억해 주신다면 얼마나 좋겠습니까!
ko.B: 주님께서 저를 스올에 숨겨 두시고, \q 주님의 진노가 지나갈 때까지 저를 감추어 두셨다가, \q 때를 정해 저를 기억해 주시면 좋겠습니다!
ko.R: 주님께서 저를 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳에 숨겨 주시면 좋겠습니다. \q 주님의 노여움이 풀리실 때까지 저를 거기 두셨다가, \q 때를 정하셔서 저를 다시 기억해 주시면 좋겠습니다.

decisions.choice: Who will give: a wish, "oh that"
decisions.reason: As in 13:5, "who will give" introduces a wish. Job turns from the hopelessness of verses 10-12 to imagine something better.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead, here as a hiding place
decisions.reason: Sheol is the realm of the dead under the earth (7:9; 11:8). Job imagines it not as the end but as a shelter where God might hide him for a time, until his anger has passed, as a person is hidden from danger (Isaiah 26:20).

decisions.choice: a limit: a set time
decisions.reason: The word (choq) is the same as "limits" in verse 5. There God set the limit of Job's life; here Job hopes God would set a time for his stay in Sheol to end.

decisions.choice: remember me: act for me again
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" someone, he turns to act for them, as he remembered Noah (Genesis 8:1) and Hannah (1 Samuel 1:19). Job hopes that God's anger would give way to care.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, as throughout the Old Testament; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

decisions.choice: "el lugar de los muertos" for Sheol at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Spanish has a plain phrase for the place of all the dead, used for Sheol at Balanced and Readable through the poetic books; Literal keeps "el Seol".

decisions.choice: « le séjour des morts » for Sheol at Balanced and Readable
alternatives: « la tombe » (as the English Readable "the grave")
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of all the dead, not one person's grave; French has a plain, well-known phrase for it, used for Sheol at both Balanced and Readable through the poetic books. Literal keeps « le Shéol ».

source.text: אִם־יָמ֥וּת גֶּ֗בֶר הֲיִ֫חְיֶ֥ה כָּל־יְמֵ֣י צְבָאִ֣י אֲיַחֵ֑ל עַד־בּ֝֗וֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: If dies a man, will he live? All [the] days of my service I would wait until comes my relief.

en.L: If {{gender:a mortal|a man}} dies, will {{gender:they|he}} live [again]? \q All the days of my hard service I would wait, \q until my relief should come.
en.B: If {{gender:a mortal|a man}} dies, will {{gender:they|he}} live again? \q All the days of my hard service I would wait \q until my release came.
en.R: If people die, will they live again? \q I would wait through all my days of hard service \q until my release came.

es.L: Si {{gender:el mortal|el hombre}} muere, ¿vivirá [otra vez]? \q Todos los días de mi servicio esperaría, \q hasta que llegara mi relevo.
es.B: Si {{gender:el mortal|el hombre}} muere, ¿volverá a vivir? \q Todos los días de mi duro servicio esperaría \q hasta que llegara mi liberación.
es.R: Si las personas mueren, ¿vuelven a vivir? \q Esperaría todos los días de mi duro servicio \q hasta que llegara mi liberación.

fr.L: Si {{gender:le mortel|l’homme}} meurt, vivra-t-il [de nouveau] ? \q Tous les jours de mon dur service, j’attendrais, \q jusqu’à ce que vienne ma relève.
fr.B: Si {{gender:le mortel|l’homme}} meurt, revivra-t-il ? \q Tous les jours de mon dur service, j’attendrais \q que vienne ma libération.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un meurt, peut-il revivre ? \q J’attendrais pendant tous mes jours de dur service, \q jusqu’à ce que ma libération arrive.

sw.L: Mtu akifa, je, ataishi [tena]? \q Siku zote za utumishi wangu mgumu ningengoja, \q mpaka badiliko langu lije.
sw.B: Mtu akifa, je, ataishi tena? \q Siku zote za utumishi wangu mzito ningesubiri \q mpaka kuachiliwa kwangu kufike.
sw.R: Watu wakifa, je, wataishi tena? \q Ningesubiri siku zote za utumishi wangu mgumu \q mpaka nifunguliwe.

vi.L: Nếu con người chết, [họ] sẽ sống lại chăng? \q Trọn những ngày lao dịch của con, con sẽ chờ đợi, \q cho đến khi lúc con được thay phiên đến.
vi.B: Nếu con người chết, họ có sống lại không? \q Suốt những ngày lao dịch nặng nhọc, con sẽ chờ đợi \q cho đến khi con được giải phóng.
vi.R: Nếu người ta chết, họ có sống lại không? \q Con sẽ chờ suốt những ngày phục dịch vất vả của con \q cho đến khi con được tự do.

ko.L: 사람이 죽으면 [다시] 살겠습니까? \q 제 고된 복무의 모든 날 동안 저는 기다리겠습니다, \q 제 교대할 때가 올 때까지.
ko.B: 사람이 죽으면 다시 살 수 있겠습니까? \q 고된 복무의 모든 날 동안 \q 풀려날 때가 오기까지 저는 기다리겠습니다.
ko.R: 사람이 죽으면 다시 살아날 수 있습니까? \q 저는 고된 일을 하는 모든 날 동안 기다리겠습니다. \q 제가 풀려날 때가 올 때까지 말입니다.

decisions.choice: will he live?: an open question
decisions.reason: Job asks whether the dead can live again. Verses 10-12 seemed to say no; verses 13-15 imagine yes. The question is left open, and what follows is what Job would do if the answer were yes.

decisions.choice: service: hard service, as a soldier's term of duty
decisions.reason: The word (tsava') is used of military service and of forced labor. Job used it of human life in 7:1. Here it is his time of waiting, whether in this life or in Sheol.

decisions.choice: relief: a change, a release from duty
decisions.reason: The word (chalifah) means a change, as when a soldier on guard is relieved by another. It comes from the same root as the tree's "sprouting again" in verse 7: Job hopes for the renewal the tree has.

decisions.choice: I would wait: wait with hope
decisions.reason: The verb (yachal) is the one used in 13:15. Job would wait with expectation, not in despair.

decisions.choice: "badiliko langu" (my change)
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "sprout again" in verse 7. Literal keeps the idea of change so that the link with the tree stays visible; Balanced and Readable say what the change means for Job, his release.

source.text: תִּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ךָּ לְֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ תִכְסֹֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: You would call, and I would answer you; for [the] work of your hands you would long.

en.L: You would call, and I would answer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q for the work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would long.
en.B: You would call, and I would answer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would long for the creature {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands have made.
en.R: You would call me, and I would answer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You would long to see again the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands.

es.L: Llamarías, y yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} respondería; \q a la obra de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos añorarías.
es.B: Tú llamarías, y yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} respondería; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} anhelarías a la criatura que hicieron {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos.
es.R: Tú me llamarías, y yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} respondería. \q Desearías volver a ver al que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} hiciste con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} propias manos.

fr.L: Tu appellerais, et moi je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} répondrais ; \q l’œuvre de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la désirerais.
fr.B: Tu appellerais, et je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} répondrais ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} languirais après la créature façonnée par {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains.
fr.R: Tu m’appellerais, et je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} répondrais. \q Tu aurais envie de revoir celui que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} propres mains.

sw.L: Ungeita, nami ningekujibu; \q kazi ya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ungeitamani.
sw.B: Ungeniita, nami ningekuitikia; \q ungekitamani kiumbe kilichofanywa na mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Ungeniita, nami ningekujibu. \q Ungetamani kumwona tena yule uliyemuumba kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.

vi.L: Chúa sẽ gọi, và con sẽ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q công việc của tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ mong mỏi.
vi.B: Chúa sẽ gọi, và con sẽ đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ khao khát tạo vật do tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm ra.
vi.R: Chúa sẽ gọi con, và con sẽ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Chúa sẽ mong được gặp lại người mà chính tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dựng nên.

ko.L: 주님께서 부르시면 제가 주님께 대답하겠고, \q 주님께서는 주님 손으로 지으신 것을 그리워하실 것입니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 부르시면 제가 대답하겠습니다. \q 주님께서는 손수 지으신 피조물을 그리워하실 것입니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 저를 부르시면 제가 대답하겠습니다. \q 주님께서는 손수 만드신 저를 다시 보고 싶어 하실 것입니다.

decisions.choice: You would call ...: what would happen in that hoped-for time
decisions.reason: The verbs continue the wish of verses 13-14 and are rendered "would". In 13:22 Job asked God to call so that he could answer as in court; here the call and answer are those of friends restored to each other.

decisions.choice: long for: yearn for
decisions.reason: The verb (kasaf) means to long for deeply, as one longs for home (Genesis 31:30; Psalm 84:3). Job imagines God longing for him, not hunting him.

decisions.choice: the work of your hands: Job himself, made by God
decisions.reason: Job has already reminded God that his hands shaped and made him (10:3, 8-12). Here he hopes God will want back what he made.

decisions.choice: the creature your hands have made / the one you made
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the "work" is a person, Job himself (m3).

source.text: כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה צְעָדַ֣י תִּסְפּ֑וֹר לֹֽא־תִ֝שְׁמ֗וֹר עַל־חַטָּאתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For now my steps you would count; not you would watch over my sin.

en.L: For then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would number my steps; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would not keep watch over my sin.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would count my steps \q but would not keep watch over my sin.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would count each step I take, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would not keep watching for my sins.

es.L: Porque entonces contarías mis pasos; \q no vigilarías mi pecado.
es.B: Entonces contarías mis pasos \q pero no estarías al acecho de mi pecado.
es.R: Entonces contarías cada paso que doy, \q pero no seguirías buscando mis pecados.

fr.L: Car alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} compterais mes pas ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne surveillerais pas mon péché.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} compterais mes pas, \q mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne guetterais plus mon péché.
fr.R: Alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} compterais chacun de mes pas, \q mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne serais plus à l’affût de mes fautes.

sw.L: Kwa maana wakati huo ungehesabu hatua zangu; \q usingeichunga dhambi yangu.
sw.B: Ndipo ungezihesabu hatua zangu, \q lakini usingeiwinda dhambi yangu.
sw.R: Ndipo ungehesabu kila hatua ninayopiga, \q lakini usingeendelea kuvizia dhambi zangu.

vi.L: Vì khi ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đếm các bước con; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ không canh giữ tội con.
vi.B: Khi ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đếm từng bước con, \q nhưng không rình rập tội lỗi con.
vi.R: Khi đó Chúa sẽ đếm từng bước con đi, \q nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ không còn dò xét tội lỗi con nữa.

ko.L: 참으로 그때에는 주님께서 제 걸음을 세시고, \q 제 죄를 지켜보지 않으실 것입니다.
ko.B: 그때에는 주님께서 제 걸음을 세실지라도 \q 제 죄를 살피지는 않으실 것입니다.
ko.R: 그때에는 주님께서 제 걸음 하나하나를 세실 것입니다. \q 그러나 제 죄를 계속 찾아내려 하지는 않으실 것입니다.

decisions.choice: then you would count ... not watch: still the hoped-for time
alternatives: now you count my steps; do you not watch over my sin? (Job's present complaint)
decisions.reason: The words "for now" can carry on the hope of verses 13-15: in that time God would count Job's steps with care but would not watch for his sins. They can also turn back to the present: now God counts every step Job takes and keeps watch on his sin (13:27). The second line fits the hope better without a question, and verse 17 then speaks of sin put away. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: count my steps: watch closely over one's life
decisions.reason: To count someone's steps is to know every move they make (31:4; Psalm 56:9). In the hoped-for time this would be care, not suspicion.

source.text: חָתֻ֣ם בִּצְר֣וֹר פִּשְׁעִ֑י וַ֝תִּטְפֹּ֗ל עַל־עֲוֺנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Sealed in a bag [would be] my transgression, and you would plaster over my iniquity.

en.L: My transgression [would be] sealed up in a bag, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would plaster over my iniquity.
en.B: My offenses would be sealed up in a bag, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would cover over my guilt.
en.R: You would tie up my wrongs in a bag and seal it. \q You would cover over my sins.

es.L: Sellada en una bolsa [estaría] mi transgresión, \q y recubrirías mi iniquidad.
es.B: Mis ofensas quedarían selladas en una bolsa, \q y cubrirías mi culpa.
es.R: Atarías mis faltas en una bolsa y la sellarías. \q Cubrirías mis pecados.

fr.L: Scellée dans un sac [serait] ma transgression, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enduirais mon iniquité.
fr.B: Mes offenses seraient scellées dans un sac, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} recouvrirais ma faute.
fr.R: Tu attacherais mes fautes dans un sac et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le scellerais. \q Tu recouvrirais mes péchés.

sw.L: Kosa langu [lingetiwa] muhuri ndani ya mfuko, \q {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} ungeufunika uovu wangu kwa lipu.
sw.B: Makosa yangu yangefungwa ndani ya mfuko kwa muhuri, \q {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} ungeufunika uovu wangu.
sw.R: Ungeyafunga makosa yangu ndani ya mfuko na kuutia muhuri. \q Ungezifunika dhambi zangu.

vi.L: Sự vi phạm của con [sẽ] bị niêm phong trong túi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ trát kín tội ác con.
vi.B: Những lỗi lầm của con sẽ được niêm kín trong túi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ che phủ tội con.
vi.R: Chúa sẽ buộc những điều sai trái của con vào túi và niêm lại. \q Chúa sẽ che lấp tội lỗi con.

ko.L: 제 허물이 자루 속에 봉인되고, \q 주님께서 제 죄악을 덧발라 덮으실 것입니다.
ko.B: 제 허물은 자루에 넣어 봉해지고, \q 주님께서 제 죄를 덮어 주실 것입니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 제 잘못을 자루에 넣고 묶어 봉하실 것입니다. \q 제 죄를 덮어 주실 것입니다.

decisions.choice: sealed in a bag: tied up and put away
decisions.reason: A bag (tseror) was a pouch tied shut, for money or valuables (Genesis 42:35; Proverbs 7:20); sealing it closed it for good. Here it most likely means that Job's sin would be put out of sight. If verse 16 is read as a complaint, the bag would instead be the sealed record of charges kept against him.

decisions.choice: plaster over: cover, coat over
decisions.reason: The verb (tafal) is the one in 13:4, where the friends "smear" with lies. Here God would coat over Job's guilt so that it is no longer seen. Some take it as "you add to my guilt", which belongs with the complaint reading of verse 16.

decisions.choice: cover over
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the more general "cover over"; Literal keeps the picture of plaster.

source.text: וְ֭אוּלָם הַר־נוֹפֵ֣ל יִבּ֑וֹל וְ֝צ֗וּר יֶעְתַּ֥ק מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And but a mountain falling crumbles, and a rock moves from its place;

en.L: But a mountain falls [and] crumbles away, \q and a rock is moved from its place;
en.B: But as a mountain falls and crumbles away, \q and a rock is moved from its place,
en.R: But even mountains fall and crumble, \q and rocks are moved from their place.

es.L: Pero el monte que cae se desmorona, \q y la roca se mueve de su lugar;
es.B: Pero así como un monte cae y se desmorona, \q y una roca es arrancada de su lugar,
es.R: Pero hasta los montes caen y se desmoronan, \q y las rocas se mueven de su sitio.

fr.L: Mais la montagne tombe [et] s’effrite, \q et le rocher est déplacé de son lieu ;
fr.B: Mais comme une montagne tombe et s’écroule, \q comme un rocher est arraché de sa place,
fr.R: Pourtant, même les montagnes tombent et s’effritent, \q et les rochers sont déplacés.

sw.L: Lakini mlima ukianguka huporomoka, \q na mwamba huondolewa mahali pake;
sw.B: Lakini kama mlima unavyoanguka na kubomoka, \q na mwamba kuondolewa mahali pake,
sw.R: Lakini hata milima huanguka na kubomoka, \q na miamba huhamishwa mahali pake.

vi.L: Nhưng núi đổ xuống [thì] tan rã, \q và tảng đá bị dời khỏi chỗ nó;
vi.B: Nhưng như núi sụp đổ rồi tan vụn, \q như tảng đá bị dời khỏi chỗ của nó,
vi.R: Nhưng ngay cả núi cũng sụp đổ và vỡ vụn, \q và đá cũng bị dời khỏi chỗ.

ko.L: 그러나 산도 무너져 부스러지고, \q 바위도 제자리에서 옮겨지며,
ko.B: 그러나 산이 무너져 허물어지고 \q 바위가 제자리에서 밀려나듯이,
ko.R: 그러나 산조차 무너져 부서지고 \q 바위도 제자리에서 밀려난다.

decisions.choice: But: Job turns from hope back to what he sees
decisions.reason: The strong "but" ends the dream of verses 13-17. Job comes back to the hard facts of the world.

decisions.choice: mountain, rock: the most lasting things
decisions.reason: Mountains and rock stand for what does not change (9:5; Isaiah 54:10). Even these are worn down in time. Bildad later uses the same words, "a rock moved from its place" (18:4).

decisions.choice: as
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "as" to show that verses 18-19 are a comparison, completed by "so" in verse 19.

source.text: אֲבָנִ֤ים׀שָׁ֥חֲקוּ מַ֗יִם תִּשְׁטֹֽף־סְפִיחֶ֥יהָ עֲפַר־אָ֑רֶץ וְתִקְוַ֖ת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ הֶאֱבַֽדְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Stones wear away waters; wash away its torrents [the] dust of [the] land; and [the] hope of a mortal you destroy.

en.L: waters wear away stones; \q its torrents wash away the dust of the land; \q and the hope of a mortal {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy.
en.B: as water wears away stones \q and floods wash away the soil of the land, \q so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy the hope of mortals.
en.R: Water wears stones down, \q and floods wash away the soil. \q In the same way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy all our hope.

es.L: las aguas desgastan las piedras; \q sus torrentes arrastran el polvo de la tierra; \q y la esperanza del mortal {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} destruyes.
es.B: como el agua desgasta las piedras \q y las crecidas arrastran el suelo de la tierra, \q así {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} destruyes la esperanza de los mortales.
es.R: El agua desgasta las piedras, \q y las inundaciones se llevan la tierra. \q De la misma manera {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} destruyes toda nuestra esperanza.

fr.L: les eaux usent les pierres ; \q ses torrents emportent la poussière de la terre ; \q et l’espérance du mortel, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la détruis.
fr.B: comme l’eau use les pierres \q et que les crues emportent la terre du pays, \q ainsi {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruis l’espérance des mortels.
fr.R: L’eau use les pierres, \q et les inondations emportent la terre. \q De la même façon, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruis tout notre espoir.

sw.L: maji huyachakaza mawe; \q mafuriko yake huyachukua mavumbi ya nchi; \q {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} tumaini la mwanadamu unaliangamiza.
sw.B: kama maji yanavyomomonyoa mawe \q na mafuriko kuuchukua udongo wa nchi, \q ndivyo {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unavyoliangamiza tumaini la wanadamu.
sw.R: Maji humomonyoa mawe, \q na mafuriko huuchukua udongo. \q Vivyo hivyo {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaliangamiza tumaini letu lote.

vi.L: nước mài mòn đá; \q lũ của nó cuốn trôi bụi đất; \q và hy vọng của loài người, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hủy diệt.
vi.B: như nước làm mòn đá, \q như lũ lụt cuốn đi đất đai trong xứ, \q thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng hủy diệt hy vọng của loài người.
vi.R: Nước làm mòn đá, \q lũ lụt cuốn trôi đất. \q Chúa cũng hủy diệt mọi hy vọng của chúng con như vậy.

ko.L: 물은 돌을 닳게 하고, \q 그 큰물은 땅의 흙을 씻어 간다. \q 그리고 사람의 희망을 주님께서 없애십니다.
ko.B: 물이 돌을 닳게 하고 \q 큰물이 땅의 흙을 쓸어 가듯이, \q 주님께서는 사람의 희망을 꺾어 버리십니다.
ko.R: 물이 돌을 깎아 낸다. \q 홍수가 흙을 쓸어 간다. \q 그처럼 주님께서는 저희의 모든 희망을 없애 버리십니다.

decisions.choice: and you destroy the hope of a mortal: the point of the comparison
decisions.reason: The slow wearing away of mountain, rock and soil (verses 18-19) is a picture of what God does to human hope. The tree had hope (verse 7); a human being has it worn away.

decisions.choice: its torrents: downpours, floods
decisions.reason: The word (safiach) usually means what grows by itself from fallen seed (Leviticus 25:5). Here it is taken as the overflowing of water, which carries off the soil. "Its" refers back to the waters.

decisions.choice: a mortal: a frail human being
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) stresses human weakness. It is the word of 7:17, "what is a mortal, that you make so much of him?"

decisions.choice: as ... so
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the comparison of verses 18-19 explicit with "as ... so" (m1).

source.text: תִּתְקְפֵ֣הוּ לָ֭נֶצַח וַֽיַּהֲלֹ֑ךְ מְשַׁנֶּ֥ה פָ֝נָ֗יו וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: You overpower him forever, and he goes; changing his face, and you send him away.

en.L: You overpower {{gender:them|him}} forever, and {{gender:they pass|he passes}} away; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} change {{gender:their|his}} face and send {{gender:them|him}} away.
en.B: You overpower {{gender:them|him}} once for all, and {{gender:they are|he is}} gone; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} change {{gender:their|his}} face in death and send {{gender:them|him}} away.
en.R: You overpower us for good, and we pass away. \q You change how we look in death and send us away.

es.L: Lo vences para siempre, y se va; \q cambias su rostro y lo despides.
es.B: Lo dominas de una vez por todas, y se va; \q le cambias el rostro en la muerte y lo despides.
es.R: Nos vences para siempre, y desaparecemos. \q Cambias nuestro aspecto en la muerte y nos despides.

fr.L: Tu le terrasses pour toujours, et il s’en va ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} altères son visage et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le renvoies.
fr.B: Tu le terrasses une fois pour toutes, et il s’en va ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} changes son visage dans la mort et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le renvoies.
fr.R: Tu nous terrasses pour de bon, et nous disparaissons. \q Tu changes notre visage dans la mort et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous renvoies.

sw.L: Wamshinda milele, naye huenda zake; \q wabadilisha uso wake na kumfukuza.
sw.B: Unamshinda mara moja tu, naye anatoweka; \q unabadilisha uso wake katika kifo na kumwondoa.
sw.R: Unatushinda kabisa, nasi tunatoweka. \q Unabadilisha sura zetu katika kifo na kutuondoa.

vi.L: Ngài áp đảo họ mãi mãi, và họ ra đi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổi mặt họ và đuổi họ đi.
vi.B: Ngài đánh bại con người một lần đủ cả, và họ qua đời; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm biến đổi mặt họ trong sự chết rồi đuổi họ đi.
vi.R: Chúa áp đảo chúng con mãi mãi, và chúng con qua đời. \q Chúa làm biến dạng gương mặt chúng con trong cõi chết rồi đuổi chúng con đi.

ko.L: 주님께서 그를 영원히 이기시니 그가 떠나가고, \q 그의 얼굴을 변하게 하시고 그를 보내십니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 그를 단번에 꺾으시니 그가 사라지고, \q 죽음 속에서 그의 얼굴을 바꾸시고 그를 떠나보내십니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 저희를 영원히 이기시니 저희는 사라집니다. \q 죽음 속에서 저희 모습을 바꾸시고 저희를 떠나보내십니다.

decisions.choice: overpower forever: defeat once for all
decisions.reason: The verb (taqaf) means to overpower or prevail against. "Forever" (lanetsach) can also mean completely. The contest between God and a mortal ends one way.

decisions.choice: changing his face: the change death brings
decisions.reason: A face changes as death takes hold: its color and life are gone. Some see the changed face of a person in distress, but the next words, "send him away", point to death.

decisions.choice: send him away: dismiss, send off for good
decisions.reason: The verb (shalach, in this form) is used of sending someone away for good, as a wife is sent away (Deuteronomy 24:1). Death is pictured as a dismissal from life.

decisions.choice: in death
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "in death" so the sense of the changed face is clear (m2).

source.text: יִכְבְּד֣וּ בָ֭נָיו וְלֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע וְ֝יִצְעֲר֗וּ וְֽלֹא־יָבִ֥ין לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Are honored his sons, and not he knows; and they are brought low, and not he perceives it.

en.L: {{gender:Their children|His sons}} are honored, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not know [it]; \q [the children] are brought low, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not perceive it.
en.B: {{gender:Their children|His sons}} may rise to honor, but {{gender:they never know|he never knows}} it; \q {{gender:their children|his sons}} may sink low, but {{gender:they do|he does}} not see it.
en.R: Our children may be honored, but we will never know it. \q They may be disgraced, but we will not see it.

es.L: Sus hijos son honrados, y él no [lo] sabe; \q son humillados, y él no lo percibe.
es.B: Sus hijos pueden llegar a ser honrados, pero él nunca lo sabe; \q sus hijos pueden caer muy bajo, pero él no lo ve.
es.R: Nuestros hijos pueden recibir honra, pero nunca lo sabremos. \q Pueden caer en deshonra, pero no lo veremos.

fr.L: {{gender:Ses enfants|Ses fils}} sont honorés, et il ne [le] sait pas ; \q ils sont abaissés, et il ne s’en aperçoit pas.
fr.B: {{gender:Ses enfants|Ses fils}} peuvent être honorés, il n’en saura jamais rien ; \q {{gender:ses enfants|ses fils}} peuvent tomber bien bas, il ne le voit pas.
fr.R: Nos enfants peuvent être honorés, mais nous n’en saurons jamais rien. \q Ils peuvent être humiliés, mais nous ne le verrons pas.

sw.L: Wanawe huheshimiwa, naye hajui; \q hushushwa chini, naye hatambui.
sw.B: Wanawe huenda wakapata heshima, lakini yeye hajui kamwe; \q wanawe huenda wakadhalilika, lakini yeye haoni.
sw.R: Watoto wetu wanaweza kuheshimiwa, lakini hatutajua kamwe. \q Wanaweza kudharauliwa, lakini hatutaona.

vi.L: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} họ được tôn trọng, mà họ không biết; \q [con cái] bị hạ thấp, mà họ không nhận ra.
vi.B: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} họ có thể được vinh hiển, nhưng họ không hề biết; \q {{gender:con cái|con trai}} họ có thể bị sa sút, nhưng họ cũng chẳng thấy.
vi.R: Con cái chúng con có thể được tôn trọng, nhưng chúng con không bao giờ biết. \q Chúng có thể bị khinh khi, nhưng chúng con không thấy.

ko.L: 그의 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}이 존귀하게 되어도 그는 알지 못하고, \q 비천하게 되어도 그는 깨닫지 못한다.
ko.B: 그의 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}이 영예를 얻어도 그는 결코 알지 못하고, \q 그 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}이 낮아져도 그는 보지 못한다.
ko.R: 우리 자녀들이 존경을 받아도 우리는 그것을 알지 못한다. \q 자녀들이 멸시를 받아도 우리는 보지 못한다.

decisions.choice: he does not know: the dead know nothing of life on earth
decisions.reason: A person in the grave does not know what becomes of the family left behind, whether their children rise or fall (Ecclesiastes 9:5-6). For Job, who has lost all his children (1:18-19), this is part of the loneliness of death.

decisions.choice: honored, brought low: rise and fall in standing
decisions.reason: The first verb (kaved) means to be heavy, to have weight and honor; the second (tsa'ar) means to become small or insignificant (Jeremiah 30:19 sets the same two verbs side by side).

decisions.choice: his sons: his children
decisions.reason: The word (banim) means sons, and often children of both sexes. Here it stands for all the family a person leaves.

decisions.choice: [the children] / their children
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced repeat the children as the subject of the second line, so that it is clear who is brought low and who does not see it.

decisions.choice: "sus hijos" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span "sus hijos / sus hijos varones"
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, so the setting has nothing to change here, unlike the English "their children / his sons".

decisions.choice: "wanawe" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "wana" covers sons and daughters alike, so there is no second wording for the setting to choose.

source.text: אַךְ־בְּ֭שָׂרוֹ עָלָ֣יו יִכְאָ֑ב וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ עָלָ֥יו תֶּאֱבָֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Only his flesh on him feels pain, and his soul on him mourns.

en.L: Only {{gender:their own flesh feels pain for them|his own flesh feels pain for him}}, \q and {{gender:their soul mourns for them|his soul mourns for him}}.
en.B: {{gender:They feel only the pain of their own body|He feels only the pain of his own body}}; \q {{gender:they mourn only for themselves|he mourns only for himself}}.
en.R: We feel only the pain of our own bodies, \q and we mourn only for ourselves.

es.L: Solo su propia carne le duele, \q y su alma por él se lamenta.
es.B: Solo siente el dolor de su propio cuerpo; \q solo hace duelo por sí mismo.
es.R: Solo sentimos el dolor de nuestro propio cuerpo, \q y solo lloramos por nosotros mismos.

fr.L: Seule sa propre chair souffre pour lui, \q et son âme est en deuil pour lui.
fr.B: Il ne ressent que la douleur de son propre corps ; \q il ne pleure que sur lui-même.
fr.R: Nous ne sentons que la douleur de notre propre corps, \q et nous ne pleurons que sur nous-mêmes.

sw.L: Mwili wake tu humuuma, \q na nafsi yake huomboleza kwa ajili yake.
sw.B: Huhisi maumivu ya mwili wake tu; \q huomboleza kwa ajili yake mwenyewe tu.
sw.R: Tunahisi maumivu ya miili yetu tu, \q na tunajililia sisi wenyewe tu.

vi.L: Chỉ xác thịt của chính họ đau đớn cho họ, \q và linh hồn họ than khóc cho họ.
vi.B: Họ chỉ cảm thấy nỗi đau của thân xác mình; \q họ chỉ than khóc cho chính mình.
vi.R: Chúng con chỉ cảm thấy nỗi đau của thân thể mình, \q và chỉ than khóc cho chính mình.

ko.L: 오직 자기 육신만이 그를 위해 아파하고, \q 자기 영혼만이 그를 위해 슬퍼한다.
ko.B: 그는 오직 자기 몸의 아픔만 느끼고, \q 오직 자기 자신을 위해서만 슬퍼한다.
ko.R: 우리는 우리 몸의 아픔만 느끼고, \q 우리 자신만을 위해 슬퍼한다.

decisions.choice: flesh, soul: body and inner self, the whole person
decisions.reason: Flesh (basar) is the body; soul (nefesh) is the inner life. Together they mean the whole person.

decisions.choice: only ... for himself: a person's world shrinks to their own pain
alternatives: the dead still feel pain in the grave
the dying feel only their own pain
decisions.reason: "Only" and "on himself" limit what the person can feel: not the honor or shame of the children (verse 21), but only their own suffering and grief. It is not clear whether Job describes the last hours of the dying or the shadowy existence of the dead in Sheol; either way the person is shut in with their own pain.
